references.text: Jacob's blessing over Joseph contains similar language about 'the gifts of the ancient mountains' and 'the glory of the eternal heights,' reflecting Deuteronomy's poetic description of the land's blessings.
Habakkuk describes the 'eternal mountains' bowing before God, using similar terminology regarding 'ancient heights' as in Moses' blessing.
The psalm speaks of the mountains being born and the earth coming into being, linking the mountains' eternity to God's eternal nature, which relates to 'the eternal heights' in Deuteronomy.
The description of 'the eternal mountains' in connection with God's majesty and power reflects the theme of the mountains' greatness and blessing.
